title: bls12-381-fixed-g1-invert-g2: Frobenius-class rho with a cyclotomic-squaring branch priced by an itemised and measured instruction count, output Q=[x]Q0 in G2

claims.statement: For uniform nonidentity P in G1 and uniform z in GT, the algorithm in proof.md (compute g=e(P,Q0) with the pinned order pairing(Q0,P); if z=1, return Q=infinity without a walk; otherwise solve z=g^x by parallel distinguished-point Pollard rho on the 12-element Frobenius classes of GT with R=1024 twisted multipliers, a 4-Fp-multiplication canonical-conjugate key, a Granger-Scott cyclotomic-squaring branch taken with probability 35/64 (branch, multiplier and distinguished-point bits read from the free class invariant T=Re(c_0), so squaring steps need no key computation; the 12 keys are computed on multiply steps and at distinguished points only), deterministic fruitless-cycle escapes, and hard caps on steps, reports, restarts, false-fingerprint verifications and a metered total-work abort at 2^125.62 (so the work bound holds on every run); output Q=[x]Q0 in G2 and verify e(P,Q)=z) succeeds with probability at least 0.39 using at most 2^125.62 total dense-Fp12-multiplication equivalents (C=20,000), including setup, pairings, table construction, walk starts, distinguished-point handling, cycle handling, detection delay, output and verification. The per-instance pairing and the verification pairing are counted in experiment.py part F on a transcription of the pinned pairing, every field operation charged one full unit, at 10,331 units each, and the G2 output [x]Q0 at its hard maximum for a 255-bit scalar (254 doublings and 254 additions over Fp2 plus the affine encoding) at most 12,809 units; with the table and starts these setup and output items total at most 2^29.9973 units, inside the 2^31 the ledger allows. The table multiply is the reference operation (1 unit); the branch, distinguished-point and key-minimum rule is stated on the limbs as stored by the pinned blst kernels (Montgomery form x*2^384 mod p), so the priced operations read exactly the representation the rule names and no conversion is charged; the prices are those itemised in the same package (submission 747ad6c9) but charged at their own counted or analytic listing rather than at its rounded-up figures: the squaring branch is charged 9,709 AArch64 instructions per call (0.48545 unit) for a straight-line wide-lazy kernel written over blst's exported arm64 primitives, itemised as the kernel's fixed operation counts times the static instruction length of each pinned primitive body (9,319) plus the disassembled 379-instruction compiled glue body and a 10-instruction loop, 9,708 in total; that bound is cross-checked at 9,708.0022 instructions per call by Callgrind on the same compiled kernel (79,527,954 `Ir` over 8,192 calls), and the charge is the ceiling of the larger figure, replacing the audited 11,369-instruction narrow listing (9 Fp2 squarings + 34 Fp2 additions + 200 moves); the same run's control, blst_fp12_cyclotomic_sqr, measures 9,803.0018, so the compiled kernel saves 95.0 instructions by flattening its call glue, and the kernel is bit-exact against the control on 1,000 random cyclotomic elements (measured-kernel.md records the blst commit f7a88067, every operation count, static primitive length, the itemisation, the kernel source, the bit-exactness check and the Callgrind harness and record); every step carries 270 instructions of bookkeeping and multiply steps a further 2,119 instructions for the keys; distinguished-point reports go to one flat buffer of 80-byte records, sorted by the 128-bit fingerprint with eight fixed stable 16-bit radix passes and scanned for equal neighbours, at an itemised 3,831 instructions and a 4,000 charge (12 keys 2,119; two 255-bit modular multiplications 1,024; append 32; eight passes 640; scan 16), so the DP-handling term is at most 2^63.80 units and no per-report cost rests on a load factor (experiment.py part G exercises the sort and scan); the parent's charge vector (11,400 / 300 / 2,200) reproduces its own bound 2^125.7147 at its own squaring probability s=3/8 in the same cost block, and with the itemised squaring charge and s=35/64 the walk costs 0.7801140625 units per step, so the ledger total is 2^125.6197624 and the claim is 125.62. Peak memory is below 2^74 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^31 units and is included; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. The success bound relies on the standard random-mapping heuristic for rho walks, adjusted for the branch mix (effective class count N/(1-s^2-(1-s)^2/R)), with model success 0.43 against the required 0.39, supported by toy-field experiments and by running the production step rule in the real BLS12-381 GT; the firing of the abort and of the caps is covered by the heuristic H1+ (no percentage-point drift of the branch, cycle and report statistics over the run) with a budget of 0.01 of success probability; no production-size run is claimed.

experiments.purpose: Part A: on real BLS12-381 GT elements check that Re(c_0) is the same for all 12 conjugates, the Frobenius formula, the 4-multiplication conjugate-key formula, distinctness of the 12 keys, the canonical representative, the Granger-Scott squaring formula with its operation counts (9 Fp2 squarings, 34 Fp2 additions), the factorisation of r-1 and the orders of p and 2 modulo r. Part C: execute the production step rule (branch, multiplier and distinguished bits read from Re(c_0), keys only on multiply steps, twisted table, squaring, 2-cycle escape) in the real GT for thousands of steps and compare against explicit Frobenius arithmetic. Part B: run the complete algorithm (cycle escapes, distinguished points, collision solving) in a small field with the same tower shape and compare first-collision times with the random-mapping law adjusted for the branch mix. Part E: sample classes, apply one step and count image coincidences to test the pair-collision law of the branch mix. Part F: on BLS12-381 compute g=e(P,Q0) for a sampled nonidentity P with a transcription of the pinned pairing(Q0,P), check g^r=1 and g!=1, form Q=[x]Q0 in G2 for a sampled x, check Q on the G2 curve with [r]Q=O and e(P,Q)=g^x, run the identity target (Q=infinity, e(P,O)=1), and count the operations of both pairings, of each branch of the G2 doubling and addition, and of the affine encoding. Part D: recompute the work ledger, with part F's counts in the setup and output items, and the slack of the work cap. Part G: sort 4,096 seeded 128-bit fingerprints with the same eight-pass stable radix sort and scan adjacent records, checking the fixed pass count, sorted order and all 8 planted duplicate groups. Part B also reports the run-to-run fluctuation of the mean charge against the independent-steps prediction. Toy scale only; does not validate production costs.
